The '''Bimms''' were diminutive [[Near-Human]]s from the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Bimmisaari/Legends|Bimmisaari]]. The Bimms had a reputation as a peaceful, hospitable people. Sharing their homeworld with furred [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoids]] also known as the [[Bimm (furred species)/Legends|Bimm]], the two species were completely unrelated biologically, though they shared a [[Bimmini/Legends|language]] and cultural identity as Bimms. Many descriptions of Bimm culture and society ignored the biological differences between the two species. Many traveled [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] working as merchants and artists. Others remained on their homeworld, or lived in Bimm enclaves on a variety of [[Planet/Legends|planets]].

==Biology and appearance==
A [[Species/Legends|species]] of [[Near-Human]]s, the Bimm were thought to have immigrated to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Bimmisaari/Legends|Bimmisaari]] millennia in the past, assimilating into the culture of the world occupied by a furred species also known as the [[Bimm (furred species)/Legends|Bimm]]. Short in stature, the Bimm compared in height to [[Human/Legends|Human]] children, growing no taller than 1.5 meters. While comparable to younglings, males of the species frequently, and proudly, grew full beards.<ref name="AA" />

==Society and culture==
[[File:Bimm_bard_HR.png|thumb|left|200px|A Bimm bard.]]
Upon colonizing Bimmisaari, the Near-Human Bimm assimilated with the native species of Bimm, merging their culture and society into one. Though the Bimm species had lived together for almost all of their recorded history, certain aspects of their culture were more associated with one species than with another. While some sources attributed these cultural tendencies to one species or the other,<ref name="AA" /> sources such as [[Mammon Hoole]] presented them as aspects of a single, shared culture.<ref name="TEGAS">[[The Essential Guide to Alien Species (real-world book)|''The Essential Guide to Alien Species'']]</ref>

Both species called themselves simply "Bimms" and lived harmoniously with each other in their shared forest [[City/Legends|cities]], despite not sharing any biological similarities. They considered themselves to be a united people, and were considered as such by the rest of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. [[Marriage/Legends|Intermarriage]] between the two Bimm species was not uncommon, though genetic incompatibilities required such couples to adopt if they wanted children.<ref name="AA" />

Bimms were fond of art, [[Music/Legends|music]], and storytelling; their favorite stories involved heroic adventures, though they were usually content to hear the stories rather than inspire to take part in adventures themselves. The language [[Bimmini/Legends|Bimmini]], which was used by both species, was sung, rather than spoken.<ref name="AA" /> A Bimm conversation had a seemingly mystical quality, sounding to Human ears like songs being sung in five-part harmony.<ref name="HTTES">''[[Heir to the Empire Sourcebook]]''</ref>

Both species were noted for their mild-tempered, peaceful tendencies, which was the reason the two species lived together in harmony. This tendency extended to non-Bimm visitors from offworld, who would be treated as honored guests.<ref name="AA" /> The Bimm greeting ritual involved a reception line which each visitor would walk through. In complete silence, each Bimm in line would reach out and gently touch the visitor's head, arm, or back. More important visitors would attract correspondingly large crowds in the procession.<ref name="HTTE" /> This honor did not extend to armed visitors, however, who would be expected to leave their weapons behind.<ref name="HTTES" /> One of the greatest events in Bimm society was the visit of a member of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]].<ref name="UAA" /> Greatly revered by both species of Bimm, tales of Jedi such as [[Murrtaggh]] were popular among Bimm bards long after the fall of the Order.<ref name="H&R">''[[Heroes & Rogues]]''</ref> Even Bimmisaari's laws prohibiting visitors from carrying weapons were relaxed for visiting Jedi carrying [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsabers]].<ref name="HTTES" />

==History==
[[File:X_bimm2.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Two Bimms dressed in traditional garb.]]
Evolving on a world on the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]], the Bimm traveled to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Bimmisaari/Legends|Bimmisaari]] during the [[Great Manifest Period/Legends|Great Manifest Period]]. With the colonization of the world, the Bimm were introduced to the native [[Bimm (furred species)/Legends|species]] of furred [[Humanoid/Legends|Humanoids]]. Growing together as a united society the two species became known collectively as the Bimm and were well respected play-writes and experts in hospitality. During the [[Great Sith War/Legends|Great Sith War]] forces from the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] moved along the [[Lesser Lantillian Route/Legends|Lesser Lantillian Route]], upon which the Bimm homeworld was located, to mount a counteroffensive to the [[Sith Empire (Exar Kun)/Legends|Sith Empire]].<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref>

By the time of the [[New Sith Wars]], the Republic had grown significantly weaker from centuries of war, leaving the Bimm homeworld within the territory controlled by the [[Hutt Empire|Hutt regime]] and a [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] faction called the [[Brotherhood of Darkness/Legends|Brotherhood of Darkness]]. The Bimm remained under Hutt control long after the destruction of the Brotherhood, remaining in space contested by the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]].<ref name="TEA" /> Having quietly withdrawn from the corrupt Republic decades before the war, the Bimms found that their world was remote enough that few took notice of them, allowing their people to escape most of the chaos of the Republic's fall and the later oppression of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]].<ref name="HTTES" /> During the [[Sy Myrthian Insurrection]], the Bimm were conquered by the Empire and the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutts]] driven off the world.<ref name="TEGtW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> After the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], the Bimms remained neutral, but friendly toward the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] and later, the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]].<ref name="AA" /> While controlled by the [[Greater Maldrood]] as of [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], the Bimm were conquered by [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Mitth'raw'nuruodo]] in [[9 ABY/Legends|9 ABY]].<ref name="TEA" />

Around this time, agents of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa Solo]], [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] and [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] were dispatched to Bimmisaari on a peace meeting in [[9 ABY/Legends|9 ABY]] which was meant to open negotiations for the Bimms to join the Republic.<ref name="HTTE" /> The [[Shi'ido]] [[Sentientologist|anthropologist]] [[Mammon Hoole]] included an entry on the Bimms in his publication.<ref name="TEGAS" /> A major trade center, the Bimm were decimated in [[26 ABY/Legends|26 ABY]] by the [[Yuuzhan Vong]] during their [[Yuuzhan Vong War|invasion]] of the galaxy. By the end of the war, the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] made a push to free the Bimm, saving what was left of their homeworld and species from total annihilation.<ref name="TEA" /><ref name="New Jedi Order Sourcebook">''[[The New Jedi Order Sourcebook]]''.</ref>

==Bimms in the galaxy==
The Near-Human Bimms were the most frequently encountered type of Bimms in the galaxy. Working as entertainers or scholars, some Bimms became adventurers, whether as scoundrels who somehow worked their way into the circles of nobility, or as artists who followed heroes in order to witness great deeds which they could record in ballads. Entire communities of Bimms were also found in enclaves off Bimmisaari, which were noted for their hospitality.<ref name="AA" />

One Bimm who defied the pacifist Bimm norm during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]] was [[Rajah Ubooki]], a Near-Human Bimm and [[Imperial Intelligence/Legends|Imperial Intelligence]] agent who impersonated the [[Prophets of the Dark Side|Prophet of the Dark Side]] [[Kadann]], and later declared himself [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Galactic Emperor]].<ref name="END">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/member/insideronline/88/indexp2.html|text=''Evil Never Dies: The Sith Dynasties''|int=Evil Never Dies: The Sith Dynasties}}</ref> During the time of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], a group of five Bimm investors visited the [[Cularin Trade Show]], which was being held in the [[Cularin system/Legends|Cularin system]], aboard the [[Starship/Legends|starship]] ''[[TAV Prosperity]]''. During the show, the ship suffered a [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]] failure in the region of the [[Cularin comet cloud]], causing a booth to fall on the investors.<ref name="For Fun and Profit">{{LivingForce|For Fun and Profit}}</ref>

[[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] Bimms were not uncommon and many found their way into the ranks of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] throughout the world's history with the Republic. Jedi were always treated with respect in Bimm culture and celebrations were had when one visited their planet.<ref name="UAA" /> Bimm artists such as [[Ha'lathin]]<ref name="TF">''[[Tempest Feud]]''</ref> or [[Vasnish Kay]],<ref name="H&R" /> and traders and [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]] such as [[Rycar Ryjerd/Legends|Rycar Ryjerd]],<ref name="ANH">{{Film|IV}}</ref> were typical of Bimms in the galaxy.<ref name="UAA" />

==Behind the scenes==
The first depiction of a Bimm was a background character seen in the [[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina/Legends|Mos Eisley Cantina]] scenes of [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']] in [[1977]]. The character by portrayed by [[Marcus Powell]].<ref name="The Art of Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope">''[[The Art of Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope]]''</ref> In [[1979]]'s ''[[The Star Wars Holiday Special]]'', cut footage of Powell's character shot on the [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]] street set was used. Neither appearance formally named the character or his species.

The name "Bimm" first appeared in [[Timothy Zahn]]'s [[1991]] novel, ''[[Heir to the Empire]]''. [[1993]]'s ''[[Heir to the Empire Sourcebook]]'', a supplement for [[West End Games]]' ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]'' written by [[Bill Slavicsek]], described the Bimm species in more detail, and provided illustrations. While both Heir to the Empire and Heir to the Empire Sourcebook describe the Bimms as "half-furred", an illustration by [[Allen Nunis]] and [[Paul Daly]] included in Heir to the Empire Sourcebook made them appear to be simply short Humans.

In [[1995]], a [[Star Wars: Heir to the Empire (comic series)|comic book adaptation of ''Heir to the Empire'']] was published by [[Dark Horse Comics]]. The adaptation's artwork by [[Olivier Vatine]] and [[Fred Blanchard]] depicted clearly non-Human aliens with large floppy ears. The same year, however, the [[Premiere Limited]] set of the [[Star Wars Customizable Card Game|''Star Wars'' Customizable Card Game]], published by [[Decipher]], included a card identifying Powell's character from ''A New Hope'' as Rycar Ryjerd, a Bimm smuggler. Ryjerd, having been portrayed by an actor without extensive prosthetic makeup, resembled the Human-like Bimms from West End Games illustrations more closely than the floppy-eared aliens drawn by Vatine and Blanchard. 

The confusion was resolved in 1998 by [[Daniel Wallace]]'s ''[[The Essential Guide to Planets and Moons]]''. The Bimmisaari entry included a drawing of two floppy-eared Bimms, but noted that the planet was also inhabited by a small Human-like species with the same name. Later works, such as [[2001]]'s [[The Essential Guide to Alien Species (real-world book)|''The Essential Guide to Alien Species'']] by [[Ann Margaret Lewis (real person)|Ann Margaret Lewis]] and various [[Wizards of the Coast]] supplements for their ''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game]]'', went into more detail about the history and shared culture of the two Bimm species.

A later [[Retroactive continuity|retcon]] in [[Abel G. Peña]]'s [[2006]] article ''[[Evil Never Dies: The Sith Dynasties]]'' identified [[Rajah Ubooki|Kadann]], one of the main villains in the [[Adventures of a Jedi Prince|''Jedi Prince'']] series of young adult novels by [[Hollace Davids|Hollace]] and [[Paul Davids]], as a Bimm. It also explains that the Kadann in the novels was only posing as [[Kadann|the true Kadann]], a short Human. Confusion between Near-Human Bimms and Humans also appears in [[Brian Campbell]]'s [[2001]] ''Star Wars Roleplaying Game'' adventure ''[[The Rycar Run]]'', which describes Rycar Ryjerd as a Human.
